newsitem.title: UK: UK gives Shell consent for Shearwater oil/gas fiel.
newsitem.headline: UK gives Shell consent for Shearwater oil/gas fiel.

text.p: The British government on Thursday said it had given Shell UK approval to develop the North Sea Shearwater gas condensate field.
Energy minister Lord Fraser also announced consent for France's Elf Aquitaine to develop the neighbouring Elgin and Franklin gas condensate fields.
Formal approval was also passed for a new gas pipeline to Bacton, Norfolk on the east coast of England to land gas from the three fields.
The government told Shell and Elf in October that it was in favour of the pipeline.
The pipeline, named the Shearwater and Elgin Area Line (SEAL), will be the longest on the UK Continental Shelf at 463 km (288 miles).
It will carry gas from the three fields, located some 230 km (143 miles) east of Aberdeen, to the existing Shell/Esso gas terminal at Bacton.
Gas will be sent from there to the Transco National Transmission System (NTS) and to the Bacton to Zeebrugge gas interconnector.
A designed flow rate of 922 million cubic feet of gas a day will be possible through the 34-inch pipeline. Construction is expected to begin in 1998 with first gas expected to flow in 2000.
Development consent granted to Elf for the construction phase will transfer to Shell UK which will operate the pipeline and terminal during the production phase.

The Shearwater field is expected to be developed by between five and seven wells with condensate fluids being processed through a process, utilities and quarters platform linked to a fixed wellhead platform.
Estimated recoverable hydrocarbons in the 11 year life of Shearwater is 844 billion cubic feet of gas and 159 million barrels of condensate and liquids.
First production is expected in the first quarter of 2000 and output is expected to reach some 400 million cubic feet per day of gas and 90,000 barrels a day of condensates.

The Elgin field is expected to consist of a seven- well development with its own wellhead. Condensate fluids will be processed through a permanently manned process, utilities and quarters platform (PUQ) located at Elgin which will also process liquids from the Franklin field.
Franklin, located 6.5 km south east of Elgin, is expected to have five production wells tied back to a normally unattended wellhead platform.
First production from Elgin is expected in April 2000.

Estimated recoverable hydrocarbons in the 22 year life of Elgin and Franklin is 889 billion cubic feet (bcf) of gas and 244 million barrels of condensate from Elgin, and 821 bcf of gas and 123 million barrels from Franklin.

Liquids from the three fields will be transported to shore through a new 24-inch spur line into a "Y" piece near the Marnock field platform to the Eastern Trough Area Project (ETAP) pipeline from where it will proceed via the Forties system to Grangemouth in Scotland.
Provision will be made on the PUQ for a third hydrocarbon stream should a separate demand arise.
